# Code Review Report — PR #128

**Branch:** `feat/issue-121-final-editor-prose-scrubber`
**Reviewer:** Claude Sonnet 4.6 (independent sub-agent)
**Date:** 2026-04-22
**Report file:** `.github/notes/reviews/2026-04-22-pr128-claude-raw.md`

---

## Review Summary

PR #128 adds two prose-quality subagents (`prose-scrubber` and `final-editor`), a shared `final-edit` skill, two prompt templates, and coordinated documentation updates across the orchestrator, pipeline skill, and feature docs. The scope is correct, the commit messages are well-formed, and the architectural fit with the existing depth-1 nesting model is sound. Three issues require attention before merge: the story-pipeline SKILL.md resume mapping incorrectly terminates at `story_complete` when `enable_final_edit` is true, the `enable_scrubbing` config description is stale from an earlier feature iteration, and the final-editor agent spec passes a parameter to `rag-query` that the Python implementation silently ignores in query mode.

**Files Reviewed:** 11
**Findings:** 0 Critical, 2 Warning, 1 Suggestion (Documentation), 1 Warning (Correctness)

---

## Findings

### Warning Findings

```
[W-01] story-pipeline/SKILL.md resume mapping stale for `story_complete`
Category: Documentation
Severity: Warning
File: .opencode/skills/story-pipeline/SKILL.md
Lines: Resume Mapping table (approx. line 330)
Description: The resume mapping table states `story_complete → "Pipeline complete — nothing to
resume"`. With Phase 9 (`final-editor`) now wired into the pipeline and enabled via
`enable_final_edit: true`, a crash after Phase 8 leaves `story_complete` as the latest savepoint
and should resume at Phase 9, not terminate. The `docs/features/story-orchestrator.md` resume table
was updated correctly in this same PR to say "Phase 9 (Final Edit) when enabled; otherwise pipeline
complete". The SKILL.md is the canonical runtime reference that dispatched agents read; its stale
row creates a false termination signal that operators and agents will follow.
Suggestion: Update the `story_complete` row in the SKILL.md resume mapping to:
  | `story_complete` | Phase 9 (Final Edit) when `enable_final_edit` is true; otherwise pipeline complete |
```

```
[W-02] `enable_scrubbing` config description is stale in story-pipeline/SKILL.md
Category: Documentation
Severity: Warning
File: .opencode/skills/story-pipeline/SKILL.md
Lines: Config Settings Reference table, `enable_scrubbing` row
Description: The current description reads "Whether to scrub metacognition artifacts". This is
carried over from an earlier design iteration and does not describe the actual feature. The
`enable_scrubbing` flag controls the `prose-scrubber` subagent in Phase 7.5, which targets adverb
overuse, filter words, repetitive phrasing, and show-vs-tell drift. Any agent that reads this SKILL.md
to understand what the config flag does (e.g., to decide whether to dispatch `prose-scrubber`) receives
a factually wrong description that could cause incorrect dispatch decisions.
Suggestion: Update the description to:
  "Whether to run the Phase 7.5 prose-scrubber pass (adverbs, filter words, repetition, show-vs-tell)"
```

```
[W-03] `final-editor.md` passes `chapterNum: N` to `rag-query` query operation; parameter is
        silently ignored in query mode
Category: Correctness
Severity: Warning
File: .opencode/agents/final-editor.md
Lines: Workflow, step 3 (rag-query call)
Description: The final-editor workflow instructs calling `rag-query` with `operation: "query"` and
`chapterNum: N`, implying the results are filtered to chapters before chapter N. Inspection of
`src/tools/rag_query.py` `cmd_query` shows that `chapter_num` is only used when indexing
(`cmd_index`, line 75–76); the query path builds a `where_filter` from `content_type` only and does
not include `chapter_num`. Passing `chapterNum: N` on a query call has no effect — the parameter is
silently dropped. The "chapters before chapter N" scoping relies entirely on the natural-language
query string, not on any metadata filter. This is correct in practice but misleading in the spec:
implementers reading the agent definition will believe the parameter enforces the filter when it does
not. If a future rag-query update adds chapter-range filtering, the existing instruction will
coincidentally become correct; until then, it misrepresents the tool contract.
Suggestion: Remove `chapterNum: N` from the rag-query call in step 3 of the final-editor workflow,
or add an inline note: "(chapterNum is unused in query mode; result scoping is driven by query text)".
Also consider opening a follow-up issue to add `chapterNum` as a query-time `$lt` filter in
`rag_query.py` if precise pre-chapter filtering is desired.
```

### Suggestions

```
[S-01] `prose-scrubber.md` references `config.models.scrub_model` for the analysis call with
        no achievable mechanism to apply it
Category: Documentation
Severity: Suggestion
File: .opencode/agents/prose-scrubber.md
Lines: "Model Role" section and Workflow step 5
Description: The agent describes using `scrub_model` "for the analysis call when configured. If
config.models.scrub_model is absent, fall back to the default model." OpenCode subagents have no
runtime mechanism to switch their own LLM model mid-execution from a config field. The `model:`
frontmatter field is static per agent definition. The `scene-writer` tool accepts a `model` override
for revision calls, but the analysis pass (prompt-loader → agent generates JSON) is the agent's own
inference and cannot be rerouted dynamically. Neither the final-editor nor the prose-scrubber
workflow currently passes `model:` to `scene-writer` revise calls either. The `scrub_model`
instruction is therefore unreachable for the analysis step and unenforced for revision calls.
Suggestion: Choose one of:
  (a) Remove the scrub_model model-role reference from the current PR; track as a future enhancement
      once OpenCode supports dynamic model selection per step.
  (b) Restrict the scrub_model claim to revision calls only, and add explicit instruction to pass
      `model: config.models.scrub_model` to every `scene-writer` with `operation: "revise"` call.
  (c) Add a note acknowledging this is aspirational and that the analysis step uses the default model
      until dynamic routing is supported.
```

## Overall Assessment

The implementation is structurally clean and architecturally correct. Both subagents follow the established depth-1 nesting discipline, tool contracts are verified as accurate against the TS wrappers and Python tools (with one documented silent-ignore case), and the documentation coverage across SKILL.md, feature docs, and the pipeline skill is thorough. The three Warning findings each affect the correctness of a reference document that dispatched agents or operators read at runtime: the SKILL.md resume mapping and config description will cause incorrect behaviour in recovery and configuration scenarios respectively, and the misleading `chapterNum` parameter in the final-editor spec misrepresents the tool contract. All three are small, targeted fixes. The Suggestion is an inconsistency in aspirational model-routing documentation that does not affect functional correctness. The PR is recommended for merge with W-01, W-02, and W-03 resolved.
